title: Heating and cooling homes without burning gas
subtitle: State of the art for domestic heat pumps, boilers and new heating and cooling systems, with a running-cost and CO2 simulator.

whyHard.text: Heat pump efficiency falls as the gap between outdoor air and water temperature grows. Many Italian homes have radiators sized for 60–70 °C water, where a heat pump works much harder than with underfloor heating at 35 °C.

The refrigerant is changing under the installer's feet: the revised F-gas Regulation bans F-gases with GWP above 150 in small monoblock heat pumps from 2027 and removes F-gases from them entirely from 2032; split systems follow by 2035.
The natural replacement, propane (R290), is flammable, so charge limits, siting and installer training become part of the design.
Running cost depends on the ratio between the electricity price and the gas price: with the same efficiency, a high ratio can erase the savings. The simulator below shows the break-even point.
Policy is moving fast: no public incentives for stand-alone fossil fuel boilers since 1 January 2025, and a fossil-boiler phase-out planned by 2040.

technologies.name: Air-to-water heat pump
technologies.summary: Extracts heat from outdoor air and delivers it to a water circuit for heating and hot water. The central technology for low-carbon heating.
technologies.why: Mature, mass-produced, 3–5 times more efficient than a gas boiler and growing again in Europe.
limits: Efficiency drops with high flow temperatures (old radiators) and very cold weather
Outdoor unit: space, noise and condominium rules
Higher upfront cost than a boiler

technologies.name: Monoblock heat pump with natural refrigerant (R290, propane)
technologies.summary: Sealed outdoor unit charged with propane, connected to the house only by water pipes.
technologies.why: The F-gas Regulation bans F-gases with GWP above 150 in monoblock units up to 50 kW from 2027 and all F-gases below 12 kW from 2032: natural refrigerants become the standard.
limits: Flammable refrigerant: charge limits and safety distances
Fewer models for very high water temperatures

technologies.name: Heat pump paired with rooftop solar PV
technologies.summary: PV production runs the heat pump directly or through thermal storage, cutting the electricity bought from the grid.
technologies.why: Both parts are mature, and Conto Termico 3.0 covers joint installation, but the real saving depends on sizing and on how much heat is needed when the sun shines.
limits: Heating demand peaks in winter, when PV output is lowest
Needs smart control and often a storage tank to shift loads

technologies.name: Hybrid system: heat pump plus condensing boiler
technologies.summary: The heat pump covers most of the season; the boiler steps in on the coldest days or for high-temperature radiators.
technologies.why: A practical bridge for existing homes. EU guidance still allows incentives for hybrids when the renewable share is considerable, and Conto Termico 3.0 now admits add-on heat pumps next to an existing boiler.
limits: Two machines to buy and maintain
Still burns gas: the CO2 saving depends on how much heat the heat pump covers

technologies.name: Air-to-air split systems with low-GWP refrigerants
technologies.summary: Room air conditioners that also heat; the refrigerant must move to low-GWP options.
technologies.why: Ubiquitous for cooling and efficient for heating, but small air-to-air splits lose F-gases with GWP above 150 from 2029 and all F-gases by 2035, so the product range is in transition.
limits: Comfort and noise depend on the room units

technologies.name: Elastocaloric (solid-state) heat pumping
technologies.summary: Shape-memory alloys release and absorb heat when stretched and relaxed: heat pumping with no refrigerant gas.
technologies.why: Promising temperature lift among solid-state methods, but still at the prototype stage.
limits: Material fatigue over millions of cycles
Actuators and heat transfer still being engineered

technologies.name: Stand-alone condensing gas boiler
technologies.summary: The efficient end of fossil boilers, recovering heat from flue gases.
technologies.why: No public incentives for stand-alone fossil boilers since 1 January 2025, and a phase-out planned by 2040. Ecodesign rules already require at least 86% seasonal efficiency for boilers up to 70 kW.
limits: Locks in gas use and its CO2 for 15–20 years
Exposed to future gas prices and carbon pricing

technologies.name: Hydrogen boilers for homes
technologies.summary: Boilers burning hydrogen instead of methane.
technologies.why: A review of 32 independent studies found hydrogen worse than heat pumps on cost, efficiency and resources: heating with it needs about five times more electricity than a heat pump.

aiAngle.text: Predictive control that heats when electricity is cheap or PV is producing, using the building's thermal mass as storage.
Sizing assistants that estimate heat demand and the best flow temperature from bills, floor plans and climate data.
Fault detection on connected heat pumps: spotting refrigerant leaks or poor settings from operating data.
Materials discovery for solid-state heat pumping and low-GWP refrigerants.
